items.desc: The title track ‘Run For Cover’ taps into the wide-eyed escapism of the mid-’90s without slipping into nostalgia. Psychedelic details flicker across the drums like LED trails in a dark room, while a restless walking bassline gives the whole thing a wonderfully physical pull. Elements drift in and out of focus, resisting an obvious genre tag while maintaining an easy, heads-down momentum. It’s progressive music in the literal sense: constantly moving, never particularly interested in announcing where it’s going next.
items.title: [PREVIEW] Nick Warren - Run For Cover

items.desc: On “Stupa”, the mood opens outward. There’s an unmistakable Balearic quality to its sun-warmed percussion and serrated bassline,a groove that immediately suggests open-air dancefloors and late-afternoon light. A woozy synth gradually sends proceedings into more narcotic territory, while soft vocal fragments, keyboard flourishes and flashes of guitar keep one foot planted somewhere recognisably human. Nothing is hurried or overplayed. Instead, Warren lets each element breathe, resulting in the kind of patient, transportive dance music that comes from knowing exactly how little you need to do.
items.title: [PREVIEW] Nick Warren - Stupa

items.desc: Colombian DJ NAJEYS has developed a sound rooted in the melodic and hypnotic strains of progressive house. With a background in vocals and percussion, she began exploring electronic music in 2016, developing an approach to DJing that balances driving rhythms, atmospheric textures and emotive melodies. A resident at Medellín’s Club Sonorama and winner of Colombia’s Best Progressive DJ award in 2022, NAJEYS has performed at major festivals across Colombia, Mexico, Curaçao and Argentina. She next opens for Martin Garrix at Medellín’s Davi Arena on December 5th, with new music also on the horizon…
items.title: Balance Selections 388: NAJEYS

items.desc: On the optimistic ‘Hikari’, a rolling bassline drives the track forward with an infectious low-end pulse that will be difficult to ignore on the dancefloor. A stretched vocal sample drifts across uplifting melodic keys, creating a genuine feeling of space and freedom. In Japanese, hikari means “light”, a word often associated with hope, positivity and clarity. It’s a fitting title for a track that channels those exact qualities.
items.title: [PREVIEW] D-SHIFT - Hikari

items.desc: Lead cut ‘Find a Way’ draws on the genre’s classic foundations, built around a warm vocal sample and bubbling synths. A beautifully measured breakdown opens the track up, as melodic layers gather around the vocal before the groove locks back into place. It’s A-grade dancefloor material, with enough presence to become the defining moment of a set. @drunkenkongjp
items.title: [PREVIEW] D-SHIFT - Find A Way

items.desc: Celebrating his recent release with Sleep D on Butter Sessions, the elusive Mosam Howieson returns for his third BSRMIX, a 4 hour serving of pure techno power. Sink in and gear up for his live set at the Syphon Filter launch party this Saturday, October 17. (DM us for ticket access)
items.title: BSRMIX #173 - Mosam Howieson

items.desc: Sleep D and Mosam Howieson join forces for an EP that traverses peak-time pressure and deep hypnotic terrain. Opening with ‘Syphon Filter’, a monstrous techno steam train that sparked the collaboration for the record, starting over five years ago. Industrial klanging to a banging beat. Simple and effective. Chugging along, ‘Inertia’ and ‘Mirror Pool’ offer respite with a psychedelic and emotive strain of techno. Rounding out the release, Dutch producer Konduku reshapes one Mirror Pool into a stripped-back, fluid remix. Refracting the source material through his distinctive palette.
items.title: Sleep D & Mosam Howieson - Syphon Filter (Inc Konduku Remix)

items.desc: 1. This Dog Goes Subwoof 2. Sleaze 3. Rhinestones 4. Hummingbird Mabel debuts on Butter Sessions with Rhinestones, a collection of pounding progressive house excursions that lean into the deep end. Balancing blissful nostalgia with a sharp modern touch, the EP draws on classic prog and hard house sounds without getting stuck in the past. Driving rhythms, naughty amounts of low end and all the right bleeps and SFX to send your serotonin soaring. Shine on, you crazy Rhinestone.
items.title: Mabel - Rhinestones (BSRCD01)

items.desc: Welcoming back 2 of our earliest BSRMIX contributors, Luke Bruin (Mix 001) and Louis McCoy (Mix 008). Recorded live from Strawberry Fields 2025, holding down the deep sound they’re experts at whilst picking up the pace since ether inaugural BSRMIX’s from 12+ years ago. These two were an inspiration to us in the early BSR days and we’re honoured to have these selectors on mix 172.

items.desc: On The Arboretum, Analogue Attic co-founder Alex Albrecht leans further into the dancefloor, channelling the more hypnotic and driving energy that Butter Sessions is known for. Across the five tracks, listeners are treated to Albrecht's signature melody-driven deep house, bolstered by intricate rhythms, a deeper low end, and hypnotic loops designed for larger systems and later hours. The tracks are playful yet serious, functional yet full of personality. There’s the joy of long blends and the tiny details that bubble up in the mix: field recordings from time spent away, nostalgic archival mat…

items.desc: On Butter Sessions, Iti presents Colourful Choices, a collision of vivid synth melodies and fractured drum rhythms. The title nods to the multicoloured lights and patch cables of his synths - the primary source of the record's motifs. The EP opens with the title track Colourful Choices, beginning with a shimmering string-synth that bends and twists into a playful, colourful melody. It's joined by a punchy drum-machine rhythm before descending into a gritty, driving bassline. Exit shifts the energy with garage-electro edge, its weighty low-end anchoring robotic synth stabs before erupting into…

Self-described as an "amphibious, rhythmical live experience fusing analog and digital relics under a comfy skyline," BSRMIX 162 delivers exactly that. Over an hour of ambient and downtempo-leaning live electronics, recorded live at Skydiver Records in Naarm/Melbourne in early 2025.

Command D also boasts refined live sets heaving in sub-bass, while Zara's celebrated for boundary-blurring productions and her Kinesis imprint championing the local scene. On Gravity Reset, they meet in lockstep, delivering trance-inducing offerings rooted in a shared love of rhythm, space …

items.desc: Kate's debut EP 'Sprint' celebrates and cements a genre-fluid ethos with four tracks where texture and atmosphere take precedence over convention. The EP’s opener ‘Harpan’ is a bold ambient statement, brimming with otherworldly, bell-like piano riffs, humming pads, long, gliding sweeps and sparse percussion. Written in the stillness of winter, ‘Harpan’ captures the quiet beauty of solitude and anonymity amid movement. The title track ‘Sprint’ shifts gears. A synth-surge launches the track before a slow release into breakdowns, trading the opener’s introspection for unbridled motion. ‘Hoover’ …

items.desc: Club bangers, high-concept artist albums, all night long sessions and wide-ranging DJ mixes - UK talent Leon Vynehall can do it all. More than just a producer, he is a thinker who likes to explore beyond the usual limits: in the past, he's served up novellas and short films to complement his music. His most recent album, 2025's In Daytona Yellow, centred around human voices and embraced real vulnerability. This week's mix takes a similarly thoughtful approach. It was, he says, assembled like an album with an underlying musical narrative loosely themed around 'humanity'. In between the selecti…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 519 - Leon Vynehall

items.desc: Toronto's Ciel has never stuck to one sound, but what she plays is united by "various shades of dub-influenced electronic music." That is true of Slowburn, the party dedicated to slow chuggers that she has run since 2021, but also the music she's released on plenty of influential labels and the sets she plays across the world. The tempos, the timbre and texture might change as she traverses dreamy downtempo, wiggly tech house or psychedelic techno, but the warmth and sense of atmospheric pressure never do. This week's mix is about representing all of that in one ambitious two-hour trip, inclu…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 518 - Ciel

items.desc: New Delhi-raised, Bali-based DITA steps up to our podcast series with a mix of wonderfully loose and elastic rhythms drawn from her own unique colleciton. There's a steamy tropical heat to everything, from the dubby grooves to the electro-tinged breaks, breezy house and 90s rave throwbacks, all mixed with great control. It's a colourful glimpse into DITA's world in 2026, full of new finds and old favourites that reflect years of musical influences. The mix arrives as DITA's international profile continues to grow, having established herself as a resident at Potato Head Beach Club in Bali. Her…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 517 - DITA

items.desc: Amsterdam-based Hervé's endless curiosity for finding and sharing music takes him into all sorts of interesting in-between worlds. Groove and subtle progression, psychedelic swirls and deep bass are ever-present no matter where he heads, including Lentekabinet last year. As a producer, he keeps things layered and introverted, and beyond the decks he co-runs a label, event space and creative agency that help the scene to thrive. This week's mix was recorded at home in one take, on a sunny Saturday morning, and reflects the records Hervé has carried this summer while "channelling the energy tha…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 516 - Hervé

items.desc: Now Amsterdam-based, Naone was shaped in her native South Korea. Her bottomless knowledge of 90s and 00s house and techno informs the sets she plays, particularly at the No Clubs events she is closely associated with. Beyond that, she heads up the Down2Earth label and expresses herself with productions that fuse ambient textures, acid lines and dubbed-out rhythms. Dekmantel Selectors is a few days away and to get you to the starting line, Naone has dropped 90 minutes of trippy tech house. From wiggy mind-melters to shadowy chuggers and dubby rollers, it's pure heads down dancing material that…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 515 - Naone

items.desc: Dasha Rush emerged more than two decades ago but has never settled into one style. From techno sets on the main stage to more intricate experimentalism in the back room via floor-focused 12"s and a soothing ambient full-length, this self-confessed "hyperactive and neurotic" mind continues to ask questions of herself and her audiences. This weekend the FullPanda label head links with Oscar Mulero to close down the UFO stage at Dekmantel, so a mind-altering trip surely awaits anyone in attendance. As a taster before that main course, Rush has served up an hour of what she calls 'cerebral techno…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 514 - Dasha Rush

items.desc: DJs have always had to dig for records, but Nicolas Lutz has taken the search for sound to obsessive new levels. The Uruguayan has spent more than 20 years excavating tunes, labels and artists most of us never knew existed. Genre is largely irrelevant; instead, the My Own Jupiter boss threads his finds into beautifully dark and alluring soundscapes full of mystery and tension. Playing in that way requires great technical skill as well as refined taste, and this week's podcast is further proof that Lutz has both in high supply. For almost two hours here, he navigates stark and moody atmosphere…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 513 - Nicolas Lutz

items.desc: Ryan Elliott has been woven into the fabric of the underground for two decades. The Detroit native and Faith Beat label head cut his teeth back home before relocating to Berlin in 2009, where he became a core member of the Berghain and Ostgut Ton family that helped shape the sound of the contemporary scene. He has always straddled the house and techno divide, merging moods and rhythms from each into his own immersive soundscapes. Not long after a 12-hour, all-vinyl set at Berghain to mark his 50th birthday, Elliott has now selected an hour of "old, new, rare and unreleased music" and rolled i…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 512 - Ryan Elliott

items.desc: Techno heavyweights Function and Nastia Reigel first came together over a shared love of early, rave-leaning and transcendental grooves. After months swapping tunes from both the old and the new school, they got to work in the studio and, in May, dropped their Devocion EP on Dekmantel. The four tracker explores broody and melancholic techno that is doused in emotion with plenty of shadowy atmosphere and deep rolling rhythms. Off the back of that, they have now put together a mix that explores this world even further with tracks from the likes of Donato Dozzy and Regis, plus two from their own…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 511 - Function & Nastia Reigel

items.desc: Guy Blanken has been part of the Dekmantel family for almost 20 years. Under his Makam alias, he explores a light, deep and dreamy sound that contrasts with his darker work as Talismann. He recently returned to our label with the delightfully dubby house album Tarp, featuring tracks from the last 10 years, made all over the world with complete freedom. “It’s more about creating a space or a feeling than telling a specific story,” he told us recently. This July, Guy joins us in the woods for The Archive, a brand-new live show featuring plenty of treasures from his vaults. But first comes this …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 510 - Makam

items.desc: Curaçao-born sound curator Rozaly both ignites and unites the dance floor. The sounds he plays are designed to blow open preconceptions about Caribbean music and tap into a more collective sense of memory. The distillation of his musical heritage through a new contemporary lens has made him a favourite at our festivals, which is why he will join us again in Amsterdam and Croatia this summer. But first, his mix, which he describes as "a dream through the night of the Caribbean" that starts in the evening and takes you through to early morning and touches on niche styles like zess, chutney and …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 509 - Rozaly

items.desc: BASHKKA plays with a purpose beyond making people dance. The Munich-born artist is an advocate for the social and political power of electronic music and is a proud advocate of queer culture. Next to her residency at Amsterdam's Raum and Blitz Club in her hometown of Munich, she plays across the world while dropping evocative originals and remixes across the house spectrum. For this week's mix, she homes in on a seductive groove that is grounded in her own "sensual, hypnotic and driving" house music DNA. Technically mixed but full of selection flair, it's infused with glimpses of her own fort…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 508 - BASHKKA

items.desc: Alfred Anders is the sort of character every good local scene needs—collector, curator, connector, risk-taker. This week, we get a taste of his mix, cruising at 110 BPM on the slower fringes of club music. A journey through trippy, outer-space spacelines and wonderfully weird grooves, moving from early ’80s house and tribal vibes to New Beat and Proto-Techno, all anchored by his Belgian sound as a guiding red thread. Behind the decks, he is one of the main arteries of the Brussels music scene and nightscape, digging deep for unknown gems that move, entrance, and intrigue. In 10 years time he …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 507 - Alfred Anders

items.desc: Locked into the rhythm of today’s techno landscape, Berlin-based sorcerer Jesse G shapes an intense, ritualistic musical journey. This mix brings you to the depths of dark minimalism, melting into deep, psychedelic passages that become pacy and percussive before the boosters kick in and the trip gets cosmic. Her textures contain power, but never at the expense of emotional nuance, as elements of bass music, breakbeat and UK sound seep into her selections. Witness this Tresor Resident and Hard Wax staffer casting a seamless spell of punching grooves with psychedelic atmospheres at Dekmantel Se…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 506 - Jesse G

items.desc: Hailing from Düsseldorf, Time Passages label head Binh takes crate-digging dedication to another level. His ear for discovering unknown gems has made him a long-time underground favourite, often showcasing his wax during marathon-length sets in Berlin or back-to-backs with fellow cult vinyl heads. Dive into 75 minutes of his signature minimal pressure: thudding kicks and spangled synths, laced with a dark yet futuristic mood. A taste of what’s to come when Binh joins us for the 10th edition of Dekmantel Selectors on the Adriatic coast.
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 505 - Binh

items.desc: Léa Occhi is Berlin-based, Paris-rooted, but hard-wired into the dancefloor’s more introspective frequencies. The co-founder and resident of queer collective Spectrum Waves channels techno into mental, minimal rituals that are emotionally charged and deep, regardless of energy levels. Outside of the club, she's a proud champion of marginalised communities who uses music to bring people together, despite being a reserved character herself. Ahead of her appearance at Dekmantel Festival 2026, Occhi soundtracks a world where tension, groove and inward reflection collide. Supple, deeply rooted rhy…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 504 - Lea Occhi

items.desc: Amsterdam’s T.NO delivers the 503rd Dekmantel mix, giving a taste of what he’s bringing to this year’s festival season. The Rinse FM resident draws on his Surinamese heritage to weave kawina rhythms into club music with a sharp, contemporary edge. Bass-led and grounded in Afro-diasporic traditions, his productions carry a restless, exploratory energy on labels like TraTraTrax, Club Djembe and re:lax. His mix for us is a widescreen two-and-a-half-hour selection that dives deep into all aspects of his sound. After a serene ambient start, T.NO wastes no time in getting down to business and lays …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 503 - T.NO

items.desc: Our first mix of the New Year is an otherworldly back-to-back between DJ Nobu & Aurora Halal that was recorded live at Dekmantel Festival 2023. Japan's Nobu is a renowned selector with a singular but fluid approach to techno and experimental electronic music. He’s the cult figure behind the long‑running Future Terror party series and Bitta label, both of which showcase truly adventurous sounds. Halal, meanwhile, is the Brooklyn‑based favourite who runs the respected Mutual Dreaming series and has a shadowy, psychedelic style that melts genres together with experimental textures. The pair repr…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 502 - Aurora Halal & DJ Nobu

It’s the first time the 18 times Aria-winning Australian rock band has played live since its Sunsets Farewell Tour, which wrapped up in the band members’ home town of Brisbane in 2010. items.desc: The singer, songwriter, actor and advocate, who has died after a cardiac arrest while touring in Europe, kept his band’s flame burning until the end Gary “Angry” Anderson – who has died aged 79 after he was hospitalised following a cardiac arrest while on tour in Germany with the band Rose Tattoo, the balls-out band he fronted for 50 years – was not a nice boy growing up. As one of the founding members of Melbourne motorcycle club the Vigilanties, Gary Anderson initially earned the sobriquet Mouse, on account of his diminutive stature. Determined to prove himself a man, he developed a penchan…

items.desc: Though the man of the hour is unable to attend, fans flock to Rod Laver Arena and cinemas nationwide to celebrate the songs of an Australian icon At a Sydney shopping centre on a balmy Sunday evening, hundreds of people gathered to watch a concert that, according to its host, Richard Wilkins, would set a new livestreaming record for Australian cinemas. Experiencing a Rod Laver Arena event with popcorn in a cinema chair was unusual in itself – but so too was the fact that its hero, John Farnham, would not be performing, or even in attendance. Continue reading...

His 2025 album Massive Shoe is about to be re-released internationally after Young signed with the indie giant Jagjaguwar. The likes of Elton John, Djo, Zane Lowe and Elijah Wood have sung his praises. Last year he opened for Black Country New Road, Waxahatchee and MJ Lenderman on their Australian tours. With a war…

items.desc: Featuring Tom Morello, Chuck D and Idles’ Joe Talbot, the rapper’s new project celebrates the shared ideals of punk and hip-hop – ‘both the voice of the voiceless’ Adam Briggs has never been one for subtlety – in his lyrics, his punchlines or his activism. In person, the man has a huge presence. He speaks with deliberation, his voice resonating even without a microphone. Whether in front of a crowd of 80,000 or eight people, Briggs is comfortable being the focus. “I can’t hide,” he says. Not that he wants to. Continue reading...
items.title: Briggs swaps rap for punk with Big Noter: ‘I’m the same guy with the same middle finger!’

items.desc: Supporters from around Australia back the Black Wreath, a volunteer-run centre far off the beaten touring track Alice Springs has a population of 34,000 and exactly one dedicated live music space: a heavy metal venue called the Black Wreath. It has hosted hundreds of bands from around the country over the past decade – despite being 1,500km from the nearest city. For musicians in central Australia, the Black Wreath is a one-of-a-kind resource. So when its operators were informed last year of the owners’ plans to sell, they negotiated a stay of execution and began devising a fundraiser that co…
items.title: Alice Springs heavy metal music venue raises $1m in donations in fight to stay open

items.desc: Starting at 6am this Sunday, Calvin Bowman will embark on an epic feat of endurance so physically demanding he’ll have a masseur on hand to aid his recovery When Calvin Bowman really gets going on the organ, both hands fly across the keyboard in different directions and his legs pump away as each foot plays a different part on the pedal-board. During pedal solos, he has to hang on to the seat so he doesn’t fall off. We don’t think of organ players as athletes, but maybe we should: there’s a level of dexterity, coordination, muscular control and core strength involved in playing the instrument…

The 40-year-old Australian musician, who is currently on tour in North America, shared a series of Instagram Stories on Monday to explain the decision. Continue reading...

items.desc: With their bassist in palliative care for colorectal cancer, the group have a new album and two live shows to play. For Brisbane band Bugs, the moment is much more bittersweet. Last month, before the release of their fourth album, Head Noise, bass guitarist Jordan Brunoli took to Instagram with a devastating update. Diagnosed with stage-four colorectal cancer at just 29, Brunoli revealed that his treatments had been unable to stop the disease fr…
items.title: Bugs’ Jordan Brunoli is 30 and may have weeks to live – but the band are making the most of their time together

items.desc: Music has always been CARISTA’s way of finding connection. She founded United Identities in Utrecht in 2017, and it has since developed into an independent record label, events and a monthly show on NTS Radio. Her own “No Ego, All Equal” ethos sits at its centre — a belief in openness, and giving music room to find its own. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS132 CARISTA

items.desc: Fireground are known for their high energy live sets and slamming records on Tresor and Ilian Tape. This is a rare DJ mix from the duo, recorded with vinyl only. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS131 FIREGROUND

items.desc: For decades, Munich DJ Muallem has been a driving force in the city’s electronic music scene. Fresh off the closure of the Blitz club - which he co-ran as a creative force and resident for nine years - he continues to curate his own label, Childhood. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS130 MUALLEM

items.desc: Erika dreams on the cellular level, or perhaps of transdimensional intelligences moving through strange patterns on celestial objects, working towards a mysterious goal. Her connection to the dreamworld becomes concrete in her approach to music, simultaneously so solid and yet so ethereal. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS129 ERIKA

items.desc: Dialog is a Dub project by Samuel van Dijk from the Netherlands and Rasmus Hedlund from Finland. Their debut release came out on the fantastic Astral Industries in 2022 followed by a series of dope records on their own label DOT Records. Available on SoundCloud & Apple Podcasts. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS128 DIALOG

items.desc: Mareena's deep connection with electronic music began in her early teenage years in East Germany, where she experienced the quaking rise of techno. She has earned a long-standing residency (since 2012) in the techno institution Tresor and her ability to include hard and elegant elements into her vinyl-oriented sets has led her to play at renowned clubs across the globe. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS127 MAREENA

items.desc: Sun People is merging Footwork, Jungle, and Techno influences into a unique and distinctive sound that led to releases on renowned labels like Exit, Defrostatica, Rua Sound or Candy Mountain. To further expand his musical sphere he recently started a label called All Things Records that will focus on his own works and collaborative projects with like-minded musicians. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS126 SUN PEOPLE

items.desc: René Löwe, aka Vainqueur, has released highly influential records on Maurizio, Chain Reaction, and his co-founded label Scion Versions. Together with his label partner Substance, aka DJ Pete, he also performs live as Scion. A true pioneer of dub techno. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS125 VAINQUEUR

items.desc: Beatrice M. has released dope records on labels like Tectonic and Tempa. For this mix the Bait label head teamed up with Tim Reaper, Future Retro London label boss and lover of all things Jungle, Drum & Bass and Hardcore - with an impressive discography. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS124 BEATRICE M. & TIM REAPER

items.desc: London mainstay RIZ LA TEEF has been on the scene for a number of years, coming up only playing vinyl and cutting dubplates showcasing the Garage, Funky, Dubstep and Grime UK sounds. This mix is a nod to his roots as it is vinyl/dubplate only featuring his trademark smooth mixing and long blends. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS123 RIZ LA TEEF

items.desc: Aubrey has been releasing dope records for more than 30 years and has founded five labels. He also runs the Latitude record store in Berlin, and he’s still remixing, mastering, djing, and involved in all things music. It’s safe to say that he is a true legend. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS122 AUBREY

items.desc: Akua has been at the forefront of a new generation of techno connoisseurs that expertly channel the timeless energy of 90s and early 2000s into their artistry. The Ghanaian-American DJ first established herself in the influential New York underground techno world and moved to Berlin in 2023. Akua’s sets are refreshing and inspire audiences to remember the true essence of techno. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS121 AKUA

items.desc: Arthur, known for his work at Hard Wax & Open Ground, presenting a crispy take on Amapiano. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS120 ARTHUR

items.desc: This mix is a sampler for an upcoming various artists album via Tresor x Limited Network coming early next year. With music from: 5tr8tch GiGi Galaxy Sugar JPWatts Max Watts Skee Mask Available on SoundCloud and Apple Podcasts. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS119 LIMITED NETWORK

items.desc: Olgica grew up in Serbia and is now living in Austria. She throws events in both countries and beyond. Left field bass, dub, broken techno, experimental downtempo and dizziyng halftime tunes are attributes of Olgicas sets. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS118 OLGICA

items.desc: An artist with minimal online presence, Commodo is one of an increasingly rare few who make waves through the strength of their music alone. He builds bass-focused beats with soul and substance that never perpetuate a formula. Together with Gantz he just released a monster record on our ITX series. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS117 COMMODO

items.desc: INVT is the multidisciplinary art project of Luca Medici and Delbert Perez. The duo specialize in electronic music and fashion design. Luca and Delbert have grown their audience through their high energy live sets as well as their DJ sets and various independent releases that are all produced, mixed, and mastered by the two. This mix was recorded at their new party series Calentón. Enjoy! Watch the entire session: https://youtu.be/_gH9b3jsud4
items.title: ITPS116 INVT

items.desc: Tresor Resident LNS started out organizing warehouse parties in Vancouver, Canada. Since residing in Berlin her style of classic techno, house, electro and braindance can easily be identified in her studio productions and DJ sets. Her collaborations with DJ Sotofett are regularly released on Tresor Records and WANIA, while her solo productions and remixes have been released by Counter 99, Emotional Response, Freakout Cult, Sex Tags Ufo and DFA. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS115 LNS

items.desc: Reeko, also known as Architectural, started DJing in the late 90s and producing in the early 2000s, and he has released countless timeless records since. He founded the labels Mental Disorder and Evidence and was part of the PoleGroup collective for a decade. Collaborations with Surgeon, Oscar Mulero and Exium, as well as releases on many legendary labels, are part of his discography. His recent explorations on the Drum & Bass label Samurai make it clear that Juan Rico has found new ways to experiment with his sound. Available on SoundCloud & Apple Podcasts. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS114 REEKO

items.desc: Yamour has quickly gained a reputation for her versatility as a DJ, serving both House and Techno music with equal passion and finesse in her vinyl-only sets. Besides touring around the world, she is a regular guest at Giegling events and at Blitz Club in Munich. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS113 YAMOUR

items.desc: Los Angeles artist 1morning is one of the funkiest young producers in modern techno. His all-vinyl DJ sets and pumping productions on labels likes Character and Fixed Rhythms stand out. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS112 1MORNING

items.desc: Honcho is a DJ and curation trio made up of Aaron Clark, Clark Price & d'Adhemar. A pillar of the new American wave of queer underground house and techno, Honcho is a resident party at the infamous Hot Mass club in Pittsburgh and it also has become known for their annual Honcho Campout festival. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS111 HONCHO

items.desc: Berlin-based DJ and radio host Elke radiates high energy – whether through playful electro, garage, and jungle or via percussive techno, bassy rollers, and stone-cold drumfunk. She is also a resident at Open Ground in Wuppertal. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS110 ELKE

items.desc: Dub Athlete is a multi-genre artist based in Brighton. With her roots in dub and dubstep, you can hear an affinity for the minimal, psychedelic and heavyweight in her selections which span from introspective ambience to hypnotic and tribal techno, deep dubstep and dark jungle. She is a resident DJ for The Mine, and since 2019 has organised the Fortune Sessions, platforming underground dance music genres and talented local DJs. Available on SoundCloud & Apple Podcasts. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS109 DUB ATHLETE

items.desc: Pugilist is a Melbourne based producer & DJ, releasing multi genre bass music on labels like 3024, Rupture and Modern Hypnosis. Enjoy!
items.title: ITPS108 PUGILIST

items.desc: Host Evie Stokes sits down with KEXP DJ and host of the El Sonido: Cancioneros podcast, Albina Cabrera, to talk about the music that’s moving her. Tim and Jeremy discuss the various religious sources on the practitioners of spiritual jazz, from Buddhism and Hinduism to African and Gospel influences. items.desc: Love is the Message returns from our summer break just in time for the Bank Holiday Weekend, which in London means one thing: Carnival. In this episode Jeremy and Tim cover the history of Notting Hill Carnival, the largest such event in Europe. They discuss patterns of Caribbean migration to the UK, traditions of carnival from Ancient Greece to Trinidad and Rio, and the particular story of Notting Hill, with its steel bands, dub sound systems, parade and party. items.desc: Is this the way they say the future’s meant to feel? Or just 20,000 people milling about at the White Claw gazebo? This summer Tom and Chal attended a LOT of different festivals, which got us thinking about not just what makes a festival good , but what makes a festival a festival . As well as rating and slating our 2026 jollies, we look back at the half-forgotten lifestyles that birthed British festival culture in the first place, talk about our personal festival histories (guess who hates camping!) and figure out what distinguishes a proper festival from a temporary cluster of outdoor stage…
items.title: 72: When is a festival not a festival?

items.desc: Closing a hectic summer, we’re back with our regular report on the best music of the last three months. We’re joined as always by No Tags third Beatle and zillennial savant Henry Bruce-Jones to talk us through the more fried corners of his musical diet. Can he sell these stubborn uncs on DMV crime-rap, Ivorian plugg and people who simply refuse to rap on beat? Or will we just have to find our middle ground at the altar of Kwengletarianism? We’ve listed all the music that we discuss on the show below – so if one particular corner’s not your thing, it’s easy to skip along. Get the full details …
items.title: 71: Second quarter report – the best music of 2026 so far

items.desc: “Is this dubstep?” There was a time in the 2010s when approximately 23% of all YouTube comments were a variation of this question. One of the UK’s most influential yet misunderstood dance exports, dubstep is also one of those rare genres that can trace its origins to a handful of people working in a few rooms. That unusual origin story is definitively told in a new book, Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep . Based on hundreds of hours of interviews by journalist Lauren Martin, it weaves together testimony from the main players (including Benny Ill, Skream, Hatcha, Loefah, Mala, Coki, Yo…
items.title: 70: The true story of real dubstep

items.desc: Keep honking, piggies: I’m listening to whatever rockslop the algorithm just sicked up for me! So we’ve been circling a certain topic for a while now – in order to be fashionably off-cycle rather than just late to the party, of course – and we’ve finally done enough muck-raking to present you with our red-hot take. It’s verifiable: your favourite DJ is a psyop. We jest, mildly. But why is it so satisfying to point to popular things and call them a psyop? And it’s not just Geese, the perfectly solid rock band that launched a thousand hysterical thinkpieces . Angine de Poitrine? Évidemment. Rit…
items.title: 69: Your favourite DJ is a psyop

items.desc: Why be seamless when you can go KLANGGG ? This week’s guest is living proof that doing things wrong, backwards, upside-down or simply not at all can reap creative dividends. We speak, of course, about Djrum . Recorded at our book launch at London’s ICA last December, our conversation with the Oxford-dwelling DJ-producer followed up on the wild acclaim for his 2025 maybe-opus, Under Tangled Silence . The interview starts at 48:00, but before that we debrief on some new music from old favourites. Is the spirit of 2011 still haunting dance music ? We couldn’t possibly say. Look out for our third…
items.title: 68: Djrum or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Clang

items.desc: Sheffield punches well above its weight when it comes to tunes. From #1 synth-pop hits to underground techno classics, clattering industrial funk to accidental Britpop icons, the Steel City might have produced more brilliant music per capita than any other world metropolis. And yet, no one has published the definitive book on the subject – until now! Daniel Dylan Wray is one of the UK’s best music writers, and his new book Groovy, Laidback and Nasty: The History of Independent Music in Sheffield chronicles the maverick artists, chart invaders, parties, labels, venues and even Christian cults …
items.title: 67: Sheffield, Synth City

items.desc: The Q1 report is here and the charts are clear: buy underscores. 📈 On this episode of No Tags, we talk through our favourite releases of 2026 so far – not to mention some music that we’re more mixed on but felt like it was worthy of discussion regardless. Before we get into it, on 5th May we’ll be returning to 180 Studios for our second session at their audiophile listening room. Following March’s session with Call Super and Parris , this time we’ll be joined by Al Wootton and Valentina Magaletti , collaborators in Holy Tongue and live bandmates in Moin, to play records from their collections…
items.title: 66: First Quarter Report – the best music of the last three months

items.desc: We all know what sound is, but are we any good at describing it? This week’s guest is a musician, writer and one of independent music’s wisest observers. Damon Krukowski has been playing in bands since the ‘80s, drumming for dreampop originals Galaxie 500 and, for the past 30 years, fronting Damon & Naomi with his partner Naomi Yang. He’s also written three books about sound and its strange, intangible properties (most recently Why Sound Matters) and he's a proud member of UMAW, a cool young labour union for music workers. It was a privilege to talk to Damon about the full spectrum of sound –…
items.title: 65: The indies fight back! Damon Krukowski on the value of sound

items.desc: So we had another idea for a movie canon. After blinking our way through The Moment – the recent mockumentary about Charli XCX by director Aidan Zamiri – we got thinking about a certain kind of music film that exists between the margins of biopic and rockdoc. Not real, not exactly fake… and all the more incisive for it. We came up with a handful of movies – some of them HIGHLY recommended! – which dramatise rather than document the artist’s status as a ‘star’: their negotiations with fame and celebrity, their discomfort with being the centre of attention, their feelings of being trapped insid…
items.title: 64: A new film canon! Rockufiction

items.desc: Some of the most exciting dance music around right now is coming out of Baltimore. Reenergised by a younger generation of artists putting a fresh spin on the Baltimore Club sound, the city is producing stacks of great new records – and we keep hearing dazzled on-the-ground reports from our cool DJ friends (yes, we have them!) about the shows they’ve played there. Kade Young and JIALING are two of the central figures in the city’s new school, known for running events and releasing a stream of club bangers via their label WOE . They had plenty to tell us about why Baltimore is the real engine r…
items.title: 63: ⁠Baltimore is still the engine room of US club music

items.desc: Taganistas may know Lil Internet from his music videos ( Beyoncé , Diplo ), his high-concept DJ mixes , or his ever-present voice on Twitter. Since 2017 his main focus has been New Models – a website, podcast and active Discord. But the reason we asked Lil Internet to join us on No Tags is his latest music project – a brand new, rule-based genre he’s calling gencore. Showcased across two mixes released in 2024 and 2025, gencore is completely AI-generated from Udio. More controversially, Lil Internet proposes that gencore marks an evolution – or maybe even the endstate – of the hardcore contin…
items.title: 62: Lil Internet changed our minds about AI music

items.desc: Reports of the death of nightlife may be greatly exaggerated. In recent months we’ve heard of new clubs opening in Peckham and Brixton, an audio upgrade at Tola and plans for a DIY venue in Catford . Even the Old Blue Last is good again ! Yet the official figures paint a depressing picture, with hundreds of venues lost, and thousands of jobs. So which story is right? To inspect the situation, Party Lines author Ed Gillett returns to the podcast fresh from his contribution to the London Nightlife Taskforce report . The report's 23 recommendations are the result of a year-long consultation foll…
items.title: 61: Is clubbing really in decline? We asked Ed Gillett

items.desc: A stack of new interviews are coming down the No Tags pipes right now, but first we return to a conversation from our sold-out event at the ICA last month. If you couldn’t make it down, or if you were there but forgot to take notes, this episode is a keeper. London-based rave researcher Anjali Prashar-Savoie set out her vision of a ‘club commons’ – a radical, positive and participatory kind of nightlife, as inspired by her research into the history of queer scenes in the UK, from lesbian sound systems with a creche on the side to George Michael-themed free parties. The interview section begin…
items.title: 60: A radical vision for club culture with Anjali Prashar-Savoie

items.desc: Sneaking in at the last possible moment, it's the No Tags best of 2025 show! As is tradition, we’re joined by Henry Bruce-Jones to look back on the year in tunes and spotlight some lesser-feted records that you need to hear. We tried to avoid going over the same releases that we covered on the Best Music of 2025 So Far episode from July, so if you’re wondering where the love is for Smerz, aya, Jim Legxacy or numerous other albums from the first half of the year, we probably talked about them back then. Scroll down for a time-stamped rundown of the episode – the full version is available on Su…
items.title: 59: The best music of 2025

items.desc: First off, we’re plugging. The second No Tags book is here – and it looks great. ‘ Conversations on underground music culture, Volume 2 ’ compiles the best interviews and conversations we’ve had on the second year of No Tags, plus five exclusive pieces with Emma Garland , Shaad D’Souza , Mattie Colquhoun , Nono Gigsta and Yu Su . You can order it here , and it will ship from the 10th December. Speaking of plugging, No Tags live at the ICA on 11th December is almost sold out! There are around 25 tickets left. As well as live conversations with Djrum and Anjali Prashar-Savoie and a DJ set from …
items.title: 58: Deepfake Jorja and the biggest bangers of the 21st century

items.desc: …And we’re back! Yes, first episode of No Tags for a few weeks, and while we do appreciate the concern, it’s just the two of us running this show, we both have jobs that we do it around, and sometimes we get really busy. Also Tom was in Asia for three weeks and most importantly, we were making a book. That’s right: the second No Tags book is here! Titled ‘ Conversations on underground music culture, Volume 2 ’ , it’s essentially a sequel to our first book: a compendium of the best interviews and conversations we’ve had on the second year of No Tags, with five exclusive pieces to boot. You can…
items.title: 57: The second No Tags book is here!

items.desc: First, news: our new book is almost at the printers ahead of launching it at the No Tags live show in London on 11th December! We’ll be announcing our guests very soon, and you can grab tickets now from the ICA website . This week’s guest is a revered member of the UK blognoscenti: Dan Hancox . Dan has written extensively on grime (including its definitive history, Inner City Pressure ), crowds, the politics of public space and his beloved Spain, while interviewing icons from Skepta to Wiley to Barcelona’s socialist mayor . He’s also the co-host of the Cursed Objects podcast , where he and Dr…
items.title: 56: Burial whisperer Dan Hancox on grime reunions, the power of crowds and sodcasting

items.desc: First, a plug: tickets are now on general sale for No Tags live at the ICA in London on 11th December! There will be special guests, and there will be a new book for sale: Vol 2 is in production now. On this week’s episode we drive headfirst – Modelos in hand – into the discourse around One Battle After Another, the designated cinema event of the year. Is it PTA’s masterpiece, or has he bitten off more than he can chew? OBAA’s ubiquity got us thinking: what was the last album that felt like a monocultural event? Do albums have the power to do this anymore, or were the early 2010s our last hur…
items.title: 55: One monoculture after another

items.desc: Lots to cover today, but first off: we’re going live again! We’ll be bringing No Tags live to the ICA in London – yep, that one – on the evening of 11th December. If you are based enough to subscribe to our paid tier, then you now have early access to discounted tickets via the link in this email’s header (and in the paywalled section at the bottom of the email). These early access tickets will be available for seven days before the show goes on general sale on 8th October. If you don’t subscribe to our paid tier but are considering making the leap, then you’re in luck: the discount will also…
items.title: 54: Flags, football shirts and indie nationalism

items.desc: We all know that hardcore will never die – but do we really know what hardcore is? As a music journalist for 15 years and raver for much longer, Holly Dicker is no stranger to documenting dance music’s heaviest, gnarliest and speediest niches – but in Dance or Die: A History of Hardcore , she attempts to finally answer that big question. From the pioneering hardware assault developed in Frankfurt and Berlin, to London’s grubbiest squat raves, Dutch intercity gabber rivalries and Scotland’s ‘tartan techno’ explosion, Dance or Die is a historical map of hardcore in its many forms. Holly dials i…
items.title: 53: Holly Dicker will be the last hardcore raver standing

items.desc: We all know what happened to the sorcerer’s apprentice, right? Mickey Mouse got hold of a spell book before he was smart enough to use it, conjured a broom that just wouldn’t quit, and nearly got sucked into a whirlpool. Yet, tragically, no one can remember what the moral of this story was supposed to be! This week we batten down the hatches in preparation for the #slopwave – at least, that was the plan a couple of months ago when we first started worrying about the volume of mass-produced AI gibberish coming down the pipes. Now it kinda feels too late? Like microplastics in the brain, we’re …
items.title: 52: Will the AI slopwave ruin music for good?

items.desc: And they said music journalism was dead. It’s list time, losers! When it comes to round-up episodes we like to draft in No Tags’ very own fifth Beatle, Henry Bruce-Jones . Minimal intro required here: we discuss our favourite music of 2025 so far, from the new wave of weird UK rappers to the changing faces of mainstream pop – plus rap oldheads, surveillance electro, minimal techno reboots and more. We didn’t include any of the records already discussed on the pod this year – including aya’s hexed and FKA twigs’ Eusexua – but they’re all still in the running for AOTY, of course. Below is a tim…
items.title: 51: The best music of 2025 so far

items.desc: Who’s on your Mount Rushmore of pop? That’s the question of the week. After welcoming Jeff Weiss back to London for a live show about his tremendous novel-slash-memoir, Waiting For Britney Spears , we got to thinking about our own pop album percies. 2007’s Blackout is certainly up there – ‘a lost weekend of one-more-gram indulgence’ that ‘embodied the hedonistic sleaze of the late Bush years,’ as Jeff sums it up in the book. Waiting For Britney… is a celebrity biography like no other – a gonzo account of Jeff’s time as a rookie in the world of Hollywood gossip rags, back when celebrities stil…
items.title: 50: Jeff Weiss is still waiting for Britney Spears

The recording is a 2 hour segments of what was an special 6 hour back to back set from label boss Alex Nut and our good friend Mr Scruff."

A look at a changing sound, where the singer, the lyrics and stories of everyday life began to move closer to the centre of the music.'

items.desc: DJ and curator Edna Martínez, from Cartagena de Indias, presents champeta, a genre born inside the picós, the sound systems of Colombia’s Caribbean coast where music is presence, tension, gathering. It carries fragmented routes shaped by circulation and bootlegs. It becomes body, dance, code, a way of occupying a space that has never been neutral. From the host: "For this Tierra Bomba Special, I bring together the champeta of Michel, Lilibeth and Edwin El Maestro. Three voices from the island, with songs from the mid-2000s to 2010. Stories of love, heartbreak, celebration and everyday life."

items.desc: Curator and DJ Edna Martinez explores the champeta, an underground musical genre and dance that originated in the Caribbean coast of Colombia in the early 1980s. The rhythms and influences are said to have arrived with the sailors from West Africa in the 1960s and 70s. We will get to know in each episode its specificities and the relevance of this scene. From the host: "A tribute to a legendary Cartagena picó El Parrandero since 1978, championing soca and Caribbean rhythms. The pure euphoria of Colombian caribbean sound system culture."

items.desc: American composer and synthesist, Pauline Anna Strom first began releasing music in the early 1980s under the moniker Trans-Millenia Consort. Working for the most part in isolation, she crafted immersive synth soundscapes, conjuring imagined worlds between ancient myth and imagined futures. After her early records fell out of circulation, her work was introduced to new audiences in 2017 through the compilation Trans-Milenia Music. She returned to releasing original work with the 2020 album Angel Tears in Sunlight, released by RVNG Intl just months after her passing.
items.title: In Focus: pauline anna strom

items.desc: Emerging from the creative crucible of LA's loose "beat scene" collective of the mid-2000s alongside fellow artists such as Ras G, Thundercat, and Nosaj Thing, Steven Ellison aka Flying Lotus took a painterly approach to the structure of hip hop production. Part of a jazz and soul lineage that includes Motown songwriter Marilyn McLeod and spiritual jazz matriarch Alice Coltrane, Ellison infused instrumentals with loose improvisational flourishes and an experimental spirit that frequently breaks beyond the definitions of hip hop. His style has expanded further incorporating R&B, jazz, IDM, and…
items.title: In Focus: Flying Lotus

items.desc: CONTENT WARNING: Racism Doubtless the most influential living American composer, Steve Reich shattered the conventions of the classical music establishment almost by accident. Taking a recording of a San Francisco street preacher, Reich played two reels simultaneously in a round, but soon discovered one machine played slower than the other, creating an endlessly complex series of irrational and rational harmonies between the two tapes. This phasing effect discovered on "It's Gonna Rain", would define Reich's career - transferring the technique into the human realm with repetitious, hypnotic a…
items.title: In Focus: Steve Reich

items.desc: In the mid 1970s, guitarist Kourosh Yaghmaei was the king of Iranian rock music - his records sold in the millions and he was internationally famous among the Iranian diaspora. But in 1979, following the Iranian revolution, his music was heavily censored and banned on the radio by the fundamentalist Iranian regime for it's psychedelic style, a sound considered too "western". Kourosh Yaghmaei's music could have been lost forever to wider audiences, but a relaxing in rules in the 1990s allowed Yaghmaei's music to be released once again. Selected by Lara Sarkissian.
items.title: In Focus: Kourosh Yaghmaei

items.desc: John Martyn, known to his family as Iain David McCready, first rose to prominence in the British folk revival scene of the mid-1960s, alongside artists like Nick Drake and Fairport Convention. "Folk" was a label Martyn always rejected, and his expansive style reflected this – there are touches of Debussy in his compositions, and his echoplex-led sustained notes were famously inspired by jazz artist Pharoah Sanders. It's perhaps ironic that Martyn's music was often so delicate - he was not. A notorious carouser, Martyn drank, and fought, and badly mistreated the women and children in his life.…
items.title: In Focus: John Martyn

items.desc: Soon after he first emerged in the mid-’50s, pianist Cecil Taylor was the most advanced improviser in jazz; five decades later he is still the most radical. Although in his early days he used some standards as vehicles for improvisation, since the early ’60s Taylor has stuck exclusively to originals. To simplify describing his style, one could say that Taylor’s intense atonal percussive approach involves playing the piano as if it were a set of drums. He generally emphasizes dense clusters of sound played with remarkable technique and endurance, often during marathon performances. Suffice it …
items.title: In Focus: Cecil Taylor

items.desc: Two hours of music from one of the greatest songwriters of the 1990s, Elliott Smith. Already a local hero in Portland with his "next big thing" band Heatmiser, Smith left the band to persue a solo career, taking the bleeding heart spirit of grunge into softer, more delicate territory. His talent for finger-picking guitar melodies and intimate, confessional lyrics proved to be a potent combination that earned him an army of obsessive fans. Selected and mixed by Smilegoth.
items.title: In Focus: Elliott Smith

items.desc: International touring DJs, record label, and longstanding Glaswegian party was founded by Jonnie Wilkes (JG Wilkes) & Keith McIvor (JD Twitch) in Glasgow in 1997. Optimo now exists as the solo project of JG Wilkes since the tragic and untimely passing of JD Twitch in September 2025. The Optimo (Espacio) NTS show, now in it's 10th year, exhibits a unique disregard for genres and musical restrictions, striking out into often head-messing territories - from the "sublime to the ridiculous" - oddball electronic, Post Punk rarities, 4th World, EBM, Dub, Techno, Synth Pop, and bags of new unreleased…

items.desc: For their collaborative full-length debut, Eris Drew and Octo Octa hunkered down in their New Hampshire cabin to craft a celebratory, sample-heavy tribute to the maximalist dance music of yore.
items.title: Alchemical Sisters

items.desc: The irreverent duo of Leo Fincham and Rowan Please plies its brilliantly digitized indie-pop bricolage on an album with the ragtag splendor of a low-budget musical.
items.title: Stick Around for Tea

items.desc: The UK selector throws caution—and genre—to the winds on an audacious 82-minute set that careens between ambient, drill’n’bass, post-punk, breakcore, and more.
items.title: DJ-Kicks

items.desc: The Philly duo’s folk music radiates a special kind of energy. Their second album is tinged with psychedelia, a wicker wunderkammer of songs, spells, and secrets.
items.title: Autosmile

items.desc: Torn between Texas and Topanga but fully herself, the songwriter sounds at home in the outlaw country idiom on an intimate, searching new record produced by Shooter Jennings.
items.title: A Mile South of Heaven

items.desc: Modeled after the literary concept of the hero’s journey, the Catalan composer’s latest album is her most ambitious yet: It’s weirder, wilder, and more dazzling than anything she’s done to date.
items.title: Dja Dja

items.desc: With new songs that rank among his very best, the Geese frontman’s solo live album is an exquisite rendering of a had-to-be-there night and a work of real-time mythmaking.
items.title: Live at Carnegie Hall

items.desc: The UK artist brings a frenzy of club-grime provocation and internet humor to his glitched-out emo, but his portrayal of small-town malaise is what makes it a riot.
items.title: THIS IS SPA TOWN!

items.desc: Tinashe’s eighth album is her best and bravest yet: more ambitious, more focused, and effortlessly in touch with the zeitgeist. It’s the best pop album of the year.
items.title: Popstar

items.desc: Exploding its signature blend of noise-punk and dance music to masterful extremes, the Irish band gets louder, rawer, funnier, and more methodical on its exhilarating fourth album.
items.title: Pugnello

items.desc: Earnest and disaffected, ironic and confrontational, the Brooklyn songwriter’s Sub Pop debut channels trans rage into scrappy DIY punk with no patience left.
items.title: Ultimate Love Forever

items.desc: Kurt Wagner reinvents his band yet again, this time slimming down to a bare-bones acoustic setup and stripping away the studio artifice. But his storytelling remains as expansive as ever.
items.title: Punching the Clown

items.desc: The experimental Brooklyn project returns with a serene and spectral new album, using an ever-shifting musical backdrop to explore themes of illusion and doubt.
items.title: fata morgana

items.desc: For her third solo album, Phoebe Bridgers expands and contracts, capturing experiences that are strange, solitary, and hers alone. It is the quietest, most cohesive record in her discography.
items.title: Lost Weekend

items.desc: There are many rappers out there who dig deep into their lives for heavy stories of pain and sorrow. The DMV rapper does this too, but he elevates the art form to a whole new level.
items.title: Somewhere Over the Rainbow

items.desc: Natal Zaks brings dub techno to a higher level on an energetic and atmospheric 2x12", another pin in the lapel of the new and outstanding Short Span label.
items.title: Uuuuuuuu

items.desc: On the follow-up to BRAT, the pop auteur pivots to a referential, proudly tossed-off rock sound that offers mystifying glances behind the curtain of stardom.

items.desc: The sixth installment of our series reexamining hip-hop in the year 2001 revisits an album about your boss, your body, your time on Earth.
items.title: The 2001 Project: Aesop Rock’s Labor Days

items.desc: The Rap-Up considers the most notable singles of the past week. Today, Donald Morrison reviews new work from Kodak Black, Cash Cobain, Rio Da Yung Og, and more.
items.title: Everyday Betrayals

items.desc: Paul Thompson considers the new short film starring the Outkast legend—and announces an exclusive POW giveaway.
items.title: Andre 3000 and the Myth of Permanence

items.desc: The Earl Sweatshirt protege’s latest album is poised and pointed.
items.title: Rappers Suck: An Interview with Cletus Strap

items.desc: The fifth installment of our series reexamining hip-hop in the year 2001 is an excerpt from Joseph Rathgeber’s Catch Us Before We Fall Off: a [ch]oral history of anticon.
items.title: The 2001 Project: cLOUDDEAD’s Self-Titled Debut

items.desc: Fifty years after Songs In The Key Of Life, four songs from Stevie Wonder’s famously impenetrable vault have been made public.
items.title: The Lost Stevie Wonder Sessions

items.desc: Questlove sat down with director and composer John Carpenter in Hollywood to discuss Cathedral , a graphic novel and heavy metal album inspired by a single dream. Carpenter tells how a bongo lesson from his father led to the iconic Halloween theme. He also talks about casting Kurt Russell after their Elvis TV movie, why The Thing was his hardest shoot, and says The Exorcist remains the scariest movie ever made. Along the way, Carpenter turns the tables and interviews Questlove, sparking a lively debate about The Beatles and whether music has reached “creative diminished returns.” It’s a funny…
items.title: John Carpenter

items.desc: In early 2022, Questlove and Team Supreme spoke to one of the most beautiful voices in all of music — Deniece Williams. She recalls her working with Stevie Wonder and Earth Wind & Fire, before breaking out into a Grammy-winning solo career that has spanned decades and multiple genres. Hear the stories behind the songs and relive the greatness. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
items.title: QLS Classic: Deniece Williams

items.desc: The Questlove Show hoped to record an episode with DJ Shadow while he was on the East Coast for the 30th-anniversary tour of Endtroducing….. , but scheduling didn’t work out this time. Instead, Open Mike Eagle—who is performing on some of Shadow’s current tour dates—and Cousin Jake celebrate Shadow’s landmark debut, its lasting impact, and more. They talk about crate-digging in dollar bins, Shadow’s little-known production work for Paris, Gift of Gab’s verse on “Midnight in a Perfect World,” and the difference between a beatmaker and a producer. They also explain why Shadow’s music demands ac…
items.title: A Quick Salute To 30 Years Of DJ Shadow's Endtroducing

items.desc: A real tycoon is in the building. Questlove sits down with Vallejo’s own E-40, the Yay Area legend who was selling records out of his trunk back when getting a major-label deal felt impossible. He built his own label, financed his projects independently, and gave Hip-Hop an entire dictionary of slang and similes. Now, with Turning My Money Over —a historic 40-song quadruple album—Earl Stevens isn’t slowing down. E-40 talks about growing up on Magazine Street in Vallejo’s Hillside neighborhood, the New York and Bay Area rappers who shaped his voice, and the year at Grambling State that taught …
items.title: E-40

items.desc: In this classic episode of Questlove Supreme from 2022, Joan Jett spoke about growing up moving between Pennsylvania, Maryland and Los Angeles, and how songs like T. Rex's "Bang a Gong" made her want to chase her dreams, even after a guitar teacher told her "girls don't play Rock & Roll." She recalls forming The Runaways as a teenager, starting with four bus rides to jam with drummer Sandy West, and the low point after the band broke up, which ended when she met Kenny Laguna and later turned a little-known Arrows B-side into the hit "I Love Rock 'n' Roll." Jett also discusses her influence on…
items.title: QLS Classic  : Joan Jett

items.desc: On this exclusive Questlove Show mini episode, Questlove talks with bass virtuoso Stanley Clarke about Last Train To Sanity , a recent 15-track album he funded himself and is selling only through his own website, with packaging designed by his daughter Natasha and full liner notes meant as a protest against streaming. Clarke also talks about recovering from a nerve injury in his arm, recording School Days at Electric Lady Studios and meeting Joey Ramone there, why he loves playing Detroit, and his plans to write an acoustic bass concerto for schools. Stay tuned for a full Stanley Clarke x epi…
items.title: QLS Mini: Stanley Clarke on His New Album, Book, Electric Lady & More

items.desc: Questlove sits down with Tame Impala’s Kevin Parker, the multi-instrumentalist from Perth—one of the most isolated cities on Earth—who spent years letting the world believe his one-man project was a band. Parker talks about turning down a big-name producer to make Innerspeaker alone in a beach shack he later bought, the more than 1,000 voice memos labeled “this will change my life,” and why he devotes 90% of his time to drum sounds. He also unpacks the idea behind Tame Impala's latest, Deadbeat , the feeling of always being on the outside—no matter how successful he becomes—and the strange wa…
items.title: Kevin Parker of Tame Impala

items.desc: Recorded in early 2020, this classic episode of Questlove Supreme is Part 2 of the Family Stand conversation. Sandra St. Victor recounts leaving Atlantic for Elektra Records, and her alleges that Sylvia Rhone shelved her intended debut LP, Sanctuary . The band also discusses Prince hearing the album and working with Sandra, Curtis Mayfield’s warm mentorship, their defiant Moon In Scorpio era, and Jeff’s incredible saxophone work on hits by Billy Ocean and Debbie Gibson. Along the way, The Family Stand share wild stories about a 1983 night at Rick James’ house and Roy Ayers on tour in Africa, …
items.title: QLS Classic: The Family Stand Part 2

items.desc: We said we’d come back for Part 2—and we did. Arthur Baker, the architect behind “Planet Rock,” “Confusion,” and so much of the ’80s dance-floor sound, returns to The Questlove Show to finish what we started nearly a year ago. Arthur takes us from carrying crates of vinyl onto airplanes to the Synclavier sessions for Hall & Oates’ Big Bam Boom , the clubs and DJs who shaped his sound, and the Brooklyn studio sessions that led to what he jokingly calls “New Arthur” records with New Order. He also opens up about Streetwise Records, the making of Beat Street , the story behind “Sun City” and Art…
items.title: Arthur Baker Part 2

items.desc: This early-2020 episode of QLS is among Questlove’s absolute favorites. The incredible trio of Sandra St. Victor, Peter Lord, and V. Jeffrey Smith joined Ahmir, Laiya, Boss Bill, and Suga Steve for a comprehensive and highly spirited two-part conversation. The result is informative, engaging, and often hilarious. Peter recalls that watching The Exorcist left him so frightened that he played the radio every night—and that’s how he discovered music. V. Jeffrey Smith reveals that his famous saxophone solo on Billy Ocean’s “Caribbean Queen” was pieced together by producer Keith Diamond from recor…
items.title: QLS Classic: The Family Stand Part 1

items.desc: In part two of Questlove’s conversation with Wallo267, the tables turn. Wallo takes over, pushing Ahmir to make some changes. They trade questions about the albums that changed their lives, ’80s jackets, Soul Train Saturdays, and the day Wallo flew to London to meet the artist whose music carried him home from prison. The result is raw, funny, and—as Questlove admits—the most public intervention he’s ever received. Wallo's latest book, Yes To You, No To Them is available now. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
items.title: Wallo267 Part 2

items.desc: In 2022, while promoting her latest book Shine Bright: A Very Personal History of Black Women in Pop , acclaimed music journalist and author Danyel Smith joined Questlove Supreme for an episode. She spoke with Questlove and Team Supreme about the book, her years leading VIBE magazine, and her experiences writing about Whitney Houston, Tupac Shakur, and Arrested Development. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
items.title: QLS Classic: Danyel Smith

items.desc: Following the Roots Picnic backstage conversation between Soulection founder Joe Kay and Questlove, Open Mike Eagle and Cousin Jake unpack the discussion and its broader significance. They trace L.A.’s beat scene from the Good Life Café through Sketchbook and Low End Theory, and examine Joe’s thoughts on Stones Throw Records’ early influence. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
items.title: A Reaction To The Joe Kay / Soulection Episode Of The Questlove Show

items.desc: Wallo267 visited The Questlove Show to discuss his latest book, Yes To You, No To Them. Instead, he ended up disrupting Ahmir’s day—in the best possible way—with an experiential pep talk that captures why so many people need this book. The acclaimed  Million Dollaz Worth of Game  co-host, motivator, and music lover looks back on his journey—one that began just across town from Questlove’s—and how misinformation led him into life-changing circumstances. The two men compare notes on life and discuss how, after a quarter century behind bars, Wallo has spent the past decade embracing freedom to t…
items.title: Wallo267 Part 1

items.desc: One of our most-played and most-beloved episodes of 2023. For Jazz Appreciation Month, Questlove and Team Supreme sat down with a living legend of the genre. Bob James recalls his incredible journey and his intersections with Sarah Vaughan, Creed Taylor, Idris Muhammad, and others. He also discusses becoming a beacon for hip-hop DJs and sample-based producers—and how he went from being a source to a collaborator with artists such as RZA, Talib Kweli, and, yes, still, Questlove. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
items.title: QLS Classic: Bob James

items.desc: Open Mike Eagle and Cousin Jake reflect on Questlove’s deep conversation with Maseo of De La Soul, pulling out its funniest reveals and heaviest emotional moments. This touches on nuggets from Gorillaz’ "Feel Good Inc." and salute the artistic integrity of scrapping big-name collabs when the music isn’t right. Along the way, they point out connections De La Soul to Bushwick Bill, Geto Boys, and ’80s Rap lore, and sit with Maseo’s vulnerability around loss, legacy, and the unseen work behind great performances. The duo also riff on the quiet comeback of CDs as fans return to tangible ways of s…
items.title: A Reaction To The Maseo Episode Of The Questlove Show

items.desc: Vince Staples sits down with Questlove for a rare, unflinching conversation about community, survival, and growing as an artist without losing yourself. Speaking about his latest album, Crybaby , Vince shares hard-earned truths and wisdom from his life, cutting through myth and memory with his trademark clarity and dark humor. The two artists explore happiness, death, faith, hobbies, and the music industry’s shifting gaze on Black artists—while tracing Vince’s journey from riding the bus to Hollywood studios to becoming one of music's sharpest minds. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy in…
items.title: Vince Staples

items.desc: As part of 2023's Jazz Appreciation Month, the incomparable Jean Carne joined Questlove Supreme. She reflected on her Atlanta upbringing and growing up around figures like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., as well as creating Spiritual Jazz in the early 1970s with her former husband, Doug Carn. Jean also shared stories from working with Earth, Wind & Fire, Phyllis Hyman, and Norman Connors—and recalls providing valuable vocal guidance to a teenage Michael Jackson. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.
items.title: QLS Classic: Jean Carne

items.desc: Questlove and Cousin Jake field some deceptively simple mailbag questions about cheesesteaks and cereal. Ahmir breaks down his fiercely loyal cheesesteak habits, giving way to tempting side quests about ketchup etiquette and Ultramagnetic MC’s memorabilia on South Street. The Q&A then pivots to music nerdery, with Ahmir naming his all-time favorite live album and dissecting what makes a live recording sonically “perfect.” He also shares the story of his first time onstage with his parents’ band as a kid. Along the way, the conversation hits bygone Philly landmarks, 2 a.m. laser tag, and what …
items.title: Philly Cheesesteaks & Escape Rooms — A Rabbit-Hole Mailbag Edition

items.desc: Questlove sits down with Soulection founder Joe Kay live backstage at the 2026 Roots Picnic in Philadelphia. The conversation traces the origins of a global movement that grew from zip files and SoundCloud posts into a worldwide community. Joe reflects on his earliest musical memories—from family deep cuts and white-label promos to discovering J Dilla—and how those influences helped shape the unmistakable Soulection sound. He and Questlove dig into the craft of DJing, from set architecture and “go-to” records to reading the room and balancing nostalgia with discovery. Joe also explains why he…
items.title: Joe Kay of Soulection

items.desc: Questlove and Team Supreme sat down with the legendary Carlos Santana in late 2021 for a wide‑ranging conversation on spirituality, music, and a lifetime of artistic risk-taking. Santana breaks down his morning gratitude ritual, his concept of grace, and how John Coltrane, Alice Coltrane, and African rhythms shaped his sound from Caravanserai through his 1970s catalog. He revisits his journey from Autlán, Tijuana, and the Bay Area to Woodstock, talks about avoiding the dark side of the ’70s Rock lifestyle, and explains why he’s committed “career suicide” multiple times in order to protect his…
items.title: QLS Classic: Carlos Santana

items.desc: In this QLS Mini, Open Mike Eagle and Cousin Jake briefly unpack their stress soundtracks, from comfort spins like XTC and R.E.M. to the way MTV and MTV News quietly raised a generation. Using their recent Kurt Loder Questlove Show interview as a springboard, they revisit formative moments like the Kurt Cobain and Tupac reports, the Real World era, and how Loder became a kind of Gen X Walter Cronkite. The conversation tracks how we used to “lean back” and receive culture versus today’s hyper-controlled feeds, while celebrating the dignity and care MTV News brought to covering cultures. See om…
items.title: A Reaction To The Kurt Loder Episode Of The Questlove Show

items.desc: Questlove and JoJo are NOT close friends. They aren’t—or at least, that’s how they approached this conversation: two pals from different genres and generations who have bonded in recent years, sitting down to see what else they might have in common. For  The Questlove Show , the two get into JoJo’s evolution from teen prodigy to Grammy-winning, multi-platinum artist—songwriting camps, vocal discipline, Broadway chops, creative blocks, and what it means to define success on your own terms. JoJo also gets real about periods of feeling low, her family, and why she’s no longer interested in traum…
items.title: JoJo

items.desc: Bruce Hornsby joined Questlove Supreme in 2020 for a deep-dive that went way beyond “The Way It Is,” tracing his late-blooming journey from Virginia jock to conservatory-trained improviser to unlikely pop star. Bruce broke down how playing with The Grateful Dead rewired his approach to live performance, why he’d spent decades upsetting soft-core fans, and how a small-town Southern upbringing informed his blunt (and progressive) songwriting about race and class. He shared wild, personal stories about mentoring Allen Iverson, getting discovered by Michael McDonald, and being the piano heartbeat…
items.title: QLS Classic: Bruce Hornsby

items.desc: In this Questlove Show mini episode, Open Mike Eagle and Cousin Jake unpack their recent sit-down with legendary producer DJ Muggs. They explore Muggs’ evolution from boom-bap architect to self-mastered, independent creator who—as he told Ahmir—built his own musical universe. The conversation digs into the so-called “drumless” beats wave, how lowering drums in the mix opens new space for MCs, and what artistic maturity and freedom really look like after decades in the game. Along the way, the two QLS affliates touch on some highlights and key points from the episode, and the power of real, in…
items.title: A Reaction To The DJ Muggs Episode Of The Questlove Show

items.desc: It's another sampler for the Quietus Low Culture Podcast, which goes out each month to our Subscriber and Subscriber Plus tier supporters . This month, tQ founders Luke Turner and John Doran cast their eyes over a controversial classic of French cinema. To access the full podcast, further information on which can be found below, you can sign up here or look for the Subscribe button on tQ's homepage. items.desc: This is a taster for the main Quietus Low Culture Podcast, released each month exclusively for our subscribers – you can find out about all the other perks they get here . "Taster' is the right word, too. Back in the stressful early days of The Quietus John and Luke would often cheer themselves up by heading to the shops to purchase the constituent parts of a ploughman's lunch – the traditional trio of bread, cheese and onions. But then, as the site expanded, so did their culinary horizons, and they branched out into Europe and beyond, inventing the French ‘homme de charrou’, the Spanish ‘ara…

items.desc: Here's your latest trailer for The Low Culture Podcast, one of the regular perks enjoyed by subscribers to The Quietus – these wonderful people fund all our work. You can find out more about subscriptions here . Sunn O)))’s original name Mars tells you something, it being both the name of a massive planetary body but also a piece of music by Gustav Holst which is a an Ur-text in the history of heavy metal, given that it is the direct musical influence on ‘Black Sabbath’ by Black Sabbath. And this is what the band did, guiding heavy metal to an irreducible, super heavy core of skull crushing r…
items.title: Low Culture Podcast sampler: Altar by Sunn O))) & Boris

This monthly show features tQ founders Luke Turner and John Doran discussing a cultural artefact that they love, from albums to films, TV shows, books... and even shoes. You can find the full archive here. The most recent podcast saw John and Luke discussing 1977 telly drama Children Of The Stones, a masterpiece of "cosmic horror" about a scientist and his who son arrive at a village in a henge that closely …
